entities.summary:
The Battle of Mycale was a pivotal conflict in which a coalition of Greek city-states, led by Pausanias of Sparta, decisively defeated the Persian Empire, marking a turning point in the Greco-Persian Wars. 

 This battle took place on September 5, 479 BCE, in Ionia, and was a crucial victory for the Greeks, who had been fighting for their independence against the Persian Empire's expansion. 

 The aftermath of the battle saw the Persians withdraw from Greece, and the Greeks gain control of the region. 

 The significance of the Battle of Mycale lies in its impact on the course of Western history, as it led to the eventual defeat of the Persian Empire and the rise of the Hellenistic period.

 The Battle of Mycale will be remembered as a testament to the bravery and determination of the Greek warriors who fought against overwhelming odds to secure their freedom.
